sentences.text: M.S. Ramachandra Rao, Chief Justice (oral)
Petitioner in this petition is complaining that road was constructed in her land in 2021 without acquiring it by the HPPWD from Lakhrehar to Kujjaballh.

She contends that on 30th September,
2021, she gave a complaint to the Chowki Incharge Sandhol, stating that the land has been excavated for the construction of road.

She contends that inspite of the same, no action has been taken to pay her compensation till date and this .
inaction is violative of Article 300-A of the Constitution of India.
Stand of the State/respondents 2.

In the reply filed by the State, it is stated that construction of rural link road referred to above was started on the demand of the people of the area including petitioner and her predecessor to get the road connectivity, and that all the land owners surrendered their land voluntarily.

It is alleged that the work was initiated during 2008 by the respondents under the PMGSY Stage-I for a total length of road about 5.00 Kms.; that this road was completed during 2008 and further work under Stage-II of the scheme was initiated in 2013 and completed in 2014.

It is stated that at no point of time,
petitioner ever raised any demand for compensation or raised any objection.
It is stated that because of the petitioner and others giving land free of cost, voluntarily, much money was saved.
It is also opposed on the ground of laches and maintainability.

3. Reliance is placed on the judgment of Supreme Court in State of Maharashtra Versus Digambar,
(1995) 4 SCC 683 and the judgment of this Court in CWP No.1966 of 2010 (Shankar Dass Versus State of H.P.)

sentences.text: It is stated that much benefit has accrued in the areas of social and economic status of the petitioner and other villages because of the construction of road.
4. It is stated that the respondents are only doing tarring work on the already constructed road and no new work has been carried out by them on the subject land.

It is also stated that demarcation was sought by the petitioner of her land and demarcation report was submitted on 10th March, 2023 and the contents thereof extracted, which indicate that substantial portion of petitioner's land was utilized for laying the road.
Consideration by the Court 5.
We have noted the contentions of both sides.
6. From the pleadings with respect to the parties, it is clear that the land of the petitioner was utilized for laying a road and no compensation was paid.

The question is whether verbal consent allegedly pleaded by the respondents can be taken into account and whether the State can be absolved of its liability to pay compensation to the petitioner, whose land was utilized for laying the road on the said ground as well as on the grounds of laches.

7. Similar issue fell for consideration before the Supreme Court in Sukh Dutt Ratra and another Versus State of Himachal Pradesh and .
others, (2022) 7 SCC 508.
8.

entities.text:
Sukh Dutt Ratra and another Versus State of Himachal Pradesh and .
others, (2022) 7 SCC 508
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In that case also, private land had been used for construction of a road in 1972-73 without initiating any proceedings for its acquisition and without paying any compensation to the land owners.
The High Court had allowed the claim of other land owners and had directed the State to initiate land acquisition proceedings, pursuant to which compensation was awarded by passing an award.

The land owners in above case relied before the High Court on the order of Himachal Pradesh High Court rendered in CWP No.816 of 1992 (Devender Singh Versus State of Himachal Pradesh) and sought similar relief.

entities.text: CWP No.816 of 1992 (Devender Singh Versus State of Himachal Pradesh)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 9. The High Court, however, had dismissed the writ petition stating that there are disputed questions of law and fact for determination on the starting point of limitation, which cannot be adjudicated in writ proceeding and gave liberty to the petitioner to file a civil suit.
10. This order was challenged in the Supreme Court.

The Supreme Court reiterated that though the right to property was no longer a fundamental right in view of the Constitution (44th amendment,
1978), the right against deprivation of property unless in accordance with procedure established by law continues to be a constitutional right under Article 300-A.
11.
It noted that the State of H.P. adopted a practice of selectively .

3 initiating acquisition proceedings and had shirked responsibility of acquiring land required for public purpose in the manner prescribed by the law.

entities.text: Pratibha Devi vs The State Of Himachal Pradesh And
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It held that the State cannot shield itself behind the ground of delay and laches and there cannot be any limitation for doing justice, because the State in a clandestine and arbitrary manner actively tried to limit the disbursal of compensation as required by law, only to those for which it was specifically prodded by the Courts, rather than all those who are entitled.
It rejected the plea of oral consent of the land owners pleaded by the State on the ground that verbal consent or lack of objection is not supported by any material on record.

It also observed that the State was unable to produce any evidence indicating that the land of the appellants therein had been taken over or acquired in the manner known to law, or that they had ever paid any compensation.
It observed that in the absence of written consent to voluntarily giving up their land, the appellants therein were entitled to compensation in terms of law.

It held following its decision in Vidya Devi Versus State of Himachal Pradesh, (2020) 2 SCC 569, that delay and laches cannot be raised in a case of continuing cause of action, or if the circumstances shock the judicial conscience of the Court.

entities.text: Vidya Devi Versus State of Himachal Pradesh, (2020) 2 SCC 569
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It reiterated that there is no period of limitation is prescribed for the Courts to exercise their constitutional jurisdiction to do such substantial justice.

It observed that forcible dispossession of a person from his private property .
without following due process of law, was violative of both his human right and constitutional right under Article 300-A.
12.

Having regard to the principles laid down in the above decisions, which apply to the instant case since no proof of petitioner voluntarily donating land is produced by the State, this writ petition is allowed and the respondents are directed to treat this subject land as having been acquired in 2021,
as is pleaded by the petitioner and pay him compensation in accordance with the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 within six months from today.
13. Pending miscellaneous application(s), if any, shall stand disposed of.
